- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early days of the 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or shows recent reversal, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >10% from prior day) and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30d moving avg), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 5+ consecutive +1.00), model often overreacts; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment is flat (all 0.00) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 3–5 day smoothing or reduce volatility penalty in forecast.
- If model forecast is consistently > true outcome by 2–3% over 3–5 days, apply downward correction in next 7–10 days, especially if sentiment is neutral or weak.
- If true outcome is below 85% of 30d moving average, model often ignores support; adjust forecast to align with recent low or 30d MA if sentiment is neutral or negative.
